hero.title: One language for global trade.
hero.lead: A shared semantic foundation for Customs, border agencies and the systems that move information across borders.

signal.title: Movement is global. Meaning has to travel with it.
signal.body: The WCO Data Model harmonizes definitions, structures and reusable information for cross-border exchange — allowing different systems and mandates to communicate without losing meaning.

executive.title: Standardize once. Reuse across the border ecosystem.
executive.body: For decision-makers, the Data Model is not another technical format. It is shared infrastructure: a way to reduce translation between systems, make requirements reusable and create a more stable foundation for digital border transformation.

points.title: Interoperability by design
points.body: Align information before implementation choices turn into integration problems.

points.title: Reuse instead of reinvention
points.body: Build on common definitions and structures across processes, agencies and initiatives.

points.title: A foundation that can evolve
points.body: Keep meaning stable while technologies, channels and implementation patterns change.

executive.statement: The value is not in making every system identical. It is in giving different systems a dependable way to understand one another.

principles.title: Invisible when it works. Essential when systems meet.

items.title: Shared vocabulary
items.body: Clear, harmonized definitions create a common semantic layer across organizations and systems.

items.title: Reusable structure
items.body: Classes, attributes and Information Packages turn a shared vocabulary into consistent information models.

items.title: Technology neutral
items.body: Meaning and structure remain stable while implementations can evolve across XML, JSON, APIs and other exchange patterns.

architecture.title: The closer you get, the more technical it becomes.
architecture.body: Start with the business context. Move through a semantic model. Finish with structures systems can implement.

layers.label: BUSINESS
layers.title: Processes & requirements
layers.body: The operational and legal context that defines what information must be exchanged.

layers.label: SEMANTIC
layers.title: Library & information model
layers.body: Definitions, classes, attributes, relationships, cardinalities and Information Packages.

layers.label: MESSAGE
layers.title: Electronic exchange
layers.body: Implementation structures for interoperable machine-to-machine exchange.

metrics.title: A working standard, not a concept.
metrics.body: Behind the shared language is a maintained technical model: reusable elements, structured classes, Information Packages and published mappings that can be implemented in real systems.
metrics.note: Prototype values. In production, these figures can be populated directly from the Data Model database.

release.status: Available in the Data Model App
release.note: Release information is externalized for this prototype. A production service could populate current and upcoming release information from an API or database.

app.title: Now enter the working layer.
app.body: The front page earns attention; the application gets work done. Core Data Model destinations stay prominent and specialist functions remain immediately available from the fixed Tools menu.

video.title: See the Data Model in context.
video.body: A short introduction to how a shared semantic foundation supports interoperability across border processes, systems and administrations.
